We've all held the shift key for a microsecond too long, or realised a mistake in the title of a post after posting, would it be possible to allow editing of titles after submission? Maybe even in a short time window, or just once only to prevent abuse of it. This is just one of those little things I find myself wanting and Im curious if anyone else thinks the same.

As long as nobody has voated the thing or commented on it, sure.

As soon as someone comments or voats on it, no matter how soon after the submission has come out, you shouldn't be able to edit the title, because then there's a possibility the title gets editorialised and users have submitted their agreement to something they didn't mean to.
I think this is fair. There should still be a time limit, but you also have to beat everyone else to it.
Having an edit history built into it aswell would also prove to be a nice feature. Doesn't hurt to see why it was edited.
In that case (no one has commented or voated on it) it would be better to delete and repost the submission. No need for lines of code to deal with something the submitter can easily do.
How about submitting a request to the mod to have the change if there is already a comment. It would appear in the mod logs which would help prevent editorializing.

After those first few minutes, the better solution I think is to delete your own post and resubmit using a better title. No mod involvement needed. A mod given the ability to alter a post title? That will be abused without a doubt.

I was thinking it could only be done if submitter sent a request for a change. Deleting and resubmitting is a simpler fix, but I was just thinking it would work if it is being edited for clarity's sake after a post already has responses. Though it may be best to resubmit anyway by then.

Same response to that idea I think.

Being able to alter a post title allows for duping users into voting for some idea at your whim. For example: make a post titled "CP ruins society" and you're guaranteed to get several upvotes by the title alone. But for "clarity's sake" you later change the post title to "CP is fun for the whole family", well then you've got several users marked as already upvoting this post and inadvertently "agreeing" that CP is good. I think you can already clarify your thoughts in self post text and edit that field as you need. The post title though - that's what users remember when keeping track of votes.
Man this would save so much time and effort.
If there's a short window of time and you can see in the post that the title was edited then I don't think there will be too much of a problem with abuse.

This is already planned and listed on Voat's GitHub repo's issue tracker:

Ability to edit title of submissions up to 5 minutes after submitting them
I like this idea, maybe allow it constantly, but allow users to see revision history? However long you'd be able to edit titles, revision history of title/body should always be available.

My depression has destroyed everything.

Looking back across my teens, twenties, and early thirties I can finally see the pattern, My depression gets me so wrapped up in difficult moments that everything else fades away and I make horrible decisions. It's cost me a lot, but nothing that wasn't something I could do without.

I know that love is easy to talk about, and it's easy to see it as more than it is. But I'm heading into middle age and have had my fair share of relationships. For two and a half years now I have been with my match. There is no better way to describe it: She is so many of the things I love about myself, and she is so much more. We had some of the best times, and then I lost my job. I allowed my depression to turn me into someone that no one want to be around, and despite her patience and commitment to me, I never made good on everything that she gave me: the chances, the love. I drove her away from me, and she in turn drove me out, and she is blameless.

I know with every bone in my body I can fix this. I owe it to myself to conquer my emotions and once again become the awesome guy I was. In doing so, I can once again become a man worthy of the best partner he could have ever asked for.

But I'm really worried. I know that the more I work on my problems, the more I will have to confront the reality of how badly I ruined everything, and that seems just terribly depressing. I guess it's just a case of things having to get better before they get worse, but I'm terrified that the process will send me back into another downward spiral, and I can't let that happen. If I can't put the piece back together, then I can't accomplish any of the goals I have set for myself.
